title: Job 10
paragraphs: ¹ My soul is sick of life. I will pour out my complaint freely; I will speak from the bitterness of my soul. ² I will say to God, "Do not condemn me — show me why you are contending with me. ³ Does it please you to oppress me, to despise the work of your own hands, while you smile on the schemes of the wicked? ⁴ Do you see as a mortal sees? Do you look on things the way humans do? ⁵ Are your days like the days of a man, your years like a man's years,

⁶ that you must search out my sin and seek out my wrongdoing? ⁷ You know that I am not guilty, and no one can rescue me from your hand. ⁸ Your own hands shaped me and made me — and now you turn and destroy me? ⁹ Remember that you formed me like clay. Will you return me to dust? ¹⁰ Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?

¹¹ You clothed me with skin and flesh, you knit me together with bones and sinews. ¹² You gave me life and showed me steadfast love, and your care has preserved my spirit. ¹³ Yet these things you hid in your heart — I know this was your purpose all along. ¹⁴ If I sinned, you would be watching, and you would not let my guilt go unpunished. ¹⁵ If I am wicked, then woe to me; and even if I am righteous, I dare not lift my head — I am so filled with shame, soaked in my own misery.

¹⁶ And if I hold my head up, you hunt me like a fierce lion, and turn your power against me once more. ¹⁷ You bring fresh witnesses against me, and your anger toward me grows — blow after blow, wave after wave of assault. ¹⁸ Then why did you bring me out of the womb? I wish I had died before any eye had seen me, ¹⁹ that I had been carried from the womb to the grave, as though I had never existed. ²⁰ The few days of my life are almost spent — leave me alone, let me have a little comfort

²¹ before I go to the place I will never return from — the land of darkness and the shadow of death, ²² a land as dark as the darkness itself, where the shadow of death covers all, where there is no order, and where the light is as dark as night.
